schema_lineage.purpose: Supplemental MQ evaluation criteria NOT addressed by the CNAPP capability schema. Scored independently, then combined via mq_scoring_mode to produce final Magic Quadrant positions for the Cloud-Native Application Protection Platform market.

cnapp_mq_gap_taxonomy_v1.0.intent: Evaluate CNAPP vendors against the 7 Magic Quadrant criteria gaps: Financial Viability, Sales Execution, Market Responsiveness, Marketing Execution, Customer Experience Quality, Market Understanding & Vision, and Vertical & Geographic Strategy. These supplement the CNAPP technical capability assessment (CSPM, CWPP, CIEM, Shift-Left, CDR, DSPM, Fringe) to complete the 15-criteria MQ evaluation framework.

metadata.framework_alignment: Gartner Magic Quadrant Evaluation Framework — G00802987 (2 July 2025); Gartner Market Guide for CNAPP

capability_scoring_scale.meaning_of_zero: No Evidence — No public data or documentation found

scoring_logic.0: No Evidence — no public data, documentation, or third-party references available.
scoring_logic.1: Minimal — vague or unsubstantiated claims only; no verifiable evidence.
scoring_logic.2: Basic — some evidence found but significant gaps remain; limited depth.
scoring_logic.3: Demonstrated — clear evidence of capability with moderate depth across multiple sources.
scoring_logic.4: Strong — well-documented with multiple proof points from credible sources.
scoring_logic.5: Market-Leading — best-in-class with extensive evidence and third-party validation.

mq_axis_mapping.note: SLE and MKE contribute to BOTH axes per Gartner MQ methodology

VIA.name: Financial Viability & Stability
VIA.focus: Overall financial health, cloud-security business unit success, and likelihood of continued CNAPP investment. Maps to MQ criterion ATE-2 (Overall Viability).

SLE.name: Sales Execution & Channel
SLE.focus: Presales and sales capabilities, hyperscaler co-sell motion, MSP/MSSP channel strategy, and CNAPP-specific marketplace reach. Maps to MQ criteria ATE-3 (Sales Execution) and COV-3 (Sales Strategy).
evidence_signals: hyperscaler co-sell tier (e.g., AWS ISV Accelerate)
free trial / cloud connector self-service signup

MKR.name: Market Responsiveness & Track Record
MKR.focus: Ability to respond to cloud-security market shifts (AI-SPM, agentless adoption, runtime convergence, multi-cloud expansion). Maps to MQ criterion ATE-4.
evidence_signals: M&A activity (e.g., Palo Alto acquiring Dig, CrowdStrike acquiring Bionic)

MKE.name: Marketing Execution & Brand
MKE.focus: Quality, creativity, and efficacy of CNAPP marketing programs plus differentiated messaging in a crowded cloud-security market. Maps to MQ criteria ATE-5 (Marketing Execution) and COV-2 (Marketing Strategy).
evidence_signals: annual flagship event (e.g., Wiz Velocity, PANW Ignite)

CXQ.name: Customer Experience Quality
CXQ.focus: Quantitative customer experience metrics for CNAPP buyers — onboarding speed for cloud connector deployment, support quality across hyperscalers, and customer success programs. Maps to MQ criterion ATE-6.

MKU.name: Market Understanding & Vision
MKU.focus: Understanding of cloud-security buyer needs, articulation of CNAPP convergence vision, and platform extensibility roadmap. Maps to MQ criteria COV-1 (Market Understanding) and COV-4 (Offering Strategy).

VIG.name: Vertical & Geographic Strategy
VIG.focus: Strategy to direct resources to regulated verticals (financial services, healthcare, public sector) and geographic regions with data sovereignty requirements. Maps to MQ criteria COV-6 (Vertical/Industry Strategy) and COV-8 (Geographic Strategy).

VIA-01.name: Revenue & Cloud-Security Growth Trajectory
VIA-01.expanded_definition: Annual revenue (total and cloud-security/CNAPP-specific where available), year-over-year ARR growth, and revenue trend over the last 3 years. Particularly important for pure-play CNAPP vendors and cloud-security business units of platform vendors.
what_to_verify_publicly: SEC filings showing cloud-security segment revenue
Press releases with ARR milestones (e.g., 'first to $500M ARR')
Analyst estimates of CNAPP market share

scoring_guidance.1: No revenue or ARR data publicly available
scoring_guidance.2: Revenue disclosed but flat or declining; or only total company revenue with no cloud-security breakdown
scoring_guidance.3: Positive growth documented; cloud-security segment identifiable; growing customer base implied
scoring_guidance.4: Strong documented growth (>30% YoY) with specific cloud-security/CNAPP revenue; clear trajectory
scoring_guidance.5: Market-leading revenue in CNAPP segment (>$500M ARR or equivalent); sustained 50%+ growth; transparent financials

VIA-02.name: Profitability & Financial Health
VIA-02.expanded_definition: Profitability indicators for the cloud-security business, burn rate (for pure-play startups like Wiz, Orca, Sysdig), cash reserves, and parent-company financial backing for platform vendors.
what_to_verify_publicly: SEC filings showing profitability or segment EBITDA
Recent funding rounds indicating runway (e.g., Wiz Series E)

scoring_guidance.1: No financial health data; high-risk funding stage with no recent rounds
scoring_guidance.2: Recent funding secured but high burn rate implied; or large company but CNAPP is a minor underfunded initiative
scoring_guidance.3: Adequate runway (2+ years) for pure-plays; stable parent backing for platform vendors; or breakeven trajectory
scoring_guidance.4: Profitable or near-profitable; strong cash position; documented commitment to sustained CNAPP R&D
scoring_guidance.5: Profitable with strong margins; investment-grade parent or unicorn-level valuation; >$1B war chest for cloud-security investment

VIA-03.name: Customer Base & Retention
VIA-03.expanded_definition: Published CNAPP / cloud-security customer count, enterprise logos, net retention rate, churn indicators, and customer base growth.
what_to_verify_publicly: G2 / Gartner Peer Insights review counts

scoring_guidance.1: No customer count or logos published
scoring_guidance.2: A few customer logos or case studies; no count or retention data
scoring_guidance.3: Published customer count (100+); multiple cloud case studies across sectors
scoring_guidance.4: Large customer base (500+); net retention data; expansion revenue documented; diverse verticals
scoring_guidance.5: 1000+ enterprise CNAPP customers; published NRR >120%; multiple Fortune 100 logos; low churn

VIA-04.name: Market Position & Competitive Standing
VIA-04.expanded_definition: Estimated CNAPP market share, inclusion in analyst CNAPP/CWPP/CSPM reports (MQ, Wave, Market Guide), competitive win rates against Wiz/Palo Alto/Microsoft, and brand recognition.
what_to_verify_publicly: Gartner MQ for CNAPP / Market Guide for CNAPP inclusion
Forrester Wave Cloud Workload Security positioning

scoring_guidance.1: No analyst recognition or competitive positioning evidence
scoring_guidance.2: Mentioned in one CNAPP analyst report or industry list
scoring_guidance.3: Included in multiple analyst reports; competitive positioning visible; moderate brand recognition
scoring_guidance.4: Named as Leader/Strong Performer in a CNAPP MQ or Wave; strong positioning against named competitors
scoring_guidance.5: Top-3 in Gartner CNAPP MQ or Forrester Wave; >10% market share; benchmark vendor cited by competitors

SLE-01.name: Cloud Marketplace & Hyperscaler Channel
SLE-01.expanded_definition: Presence on AWS / Azure / GCP marketplaces, hyperscaler co-sell tier (e.g., AWS ISV Accelerate, Azure IP Co-Sell), MSP/MSSP partner program, and technology alliances with EDR/SIEM/IAM vendors.
what_to_verify_publicly: AWS/Azure/GCP marketplace listings with private offers
Hyperscaler co-sell tier (AWS ISV Accelerate, Azure CIPP)

scoring_guidance.1: No marketplace or channel presence
scoring_guidance.2: Listed on 1 hyperscaler marketplace; minimal partner mentions
scoring_guidance.3: All 3 hyperscaler marketplaces; documented partner program; some MSSP partners
scoring_guidance.4: Co-sell tier on 2+ hyperscalers; mature partner program (50+ partners); MSSP program with named providers
scoring_guidance.5: Top co-sell tier on all 3 hyperscalers; >100 channel partners; flagship MSSP relationships; deep technology alliances

SLE-02.name: Cloud Connector Self-Service & Trial Motion
SLE-02.expanded_definition: Free trial / agentless cloud connector self-service, time-to-first-finding for prospects, sales team responsiveness, and product-led growth motion typical of modern CNAPP vendors.
what_to_verify_publicly: Free trial / 'connect your cloud in 5 minutes' availability

scoring_guidance.1: No trial or POV evidence; contact-us only
scoring_guidance.2: Demo request form only; no trial or self-service connector
scoring_guidance.3: Free trial or POV documented; cloud connector setup guide; sales team visible
scoring_guidance.4: Self-service trial with agentless cloud connector; rapid time-to-value (hours); enterprise sales overlay
scoring_guidance.5: Best-in-class PLG (sign up, connect cloud, findings in <1 hour); multi-motion sales (PLG + enterprise + channel)

SLE-03.name: Geographic Sales Coverage
SLE-03.expanded_definition: Sales presence across regions, office locations supporting cloud-security buyers, language capabilities for sales, and regional CNAPP go-to-market teams.

scoring_guidance.1: Single-region sales presence only
scoring_guidance.2: HQ region plus one additional region; limited international
scoring_guidance.3: Sales presence in 2-3 major regions; some international partners
scoring_guidance.4: Sales teams in 4+ regions; multi-language support; regional partners in each major market
scoring_guidance.5: Global sales presence; offices in all major regions; localized sales motions; 20+ country coverage

SLE-04.name: Customer Acquisition Efficiency
SLE-04.expanded_definition: Evidence of efficient CNAPP customer acquisition: cloud-risk assessments, free posture reports, ROI calculators, and demand-gen efficiency.
what_to_verify_publicly: Cloud risk assessment / free posture scan tools

scoring_guidance.1: No evidence of structured demand generation
scoring_guidance.2: Basic website lead gen; limited content marketing
scoring_guidance.3: Structured demand gen with content/events/digital; ROI calculators or risk-assessment tools
scoring_guidance.4: Multi-channel demand gen; documented short sales cycles; free cloud-risk scan as primary funnel
scoring_guidance.5: Best-in-class demand engine; documented CAC efficiency; industry-leading content velocity; community-driven growth

MKR-01.name: Product Release Cadence & Velocity
MKR-01.expanded_definition: Frequency and substance of CNAPP platform releases, feature updates, and integration of new cloud services (new AWS/Azure/GCP services, Kubernetes versions) over the last 12-24 months.

scoring_guidance.1: No release history or changelog available
scoring_guidance.2: Infrequent updates; quarterly+ releases with minor features
scoring_guidance.3: Monthly release cadence; meaningful feature additions; new cloud-service coverage documented
scoring_guidance.4: Bi-weekly releases; major capability additions; rapid coverage of new AWS/Azure/GCP services within 30-60 days of GA
scoring_guidance.5: Continuous delivery; weekly releases; same-week or same-day coverage of new cloud services; documented velocity metrics

MKR-02.name: Competitive Response to CNAPP Convergence
MKR-02.expanded_definition: Evidence of the vendor responding to CNAPP convergence trends — adding AI-SPM, DSPM, Kubernetes runtime, code-to-cloud, attack-path analysis, and runtime convergence (e.g., Wiz Defend, Sysdig CDR).
what_to_verify_publicly: Product announcements adding adjacent CNAPP capabilities

scoring_guidance.1: No evidence of market-responsive adaptations; single-pillar vendor
scoring_guidance.2: Slow to respond; capabilities lag market trends by 12+ months; missing 2+ of CSPM/CWPP/CIEM/DSPM/AI-SPM
scoring_guidance.3: Aware of trends; key capabilities added within 6-12 months of demand; covers core CNAPP pillars
scoring_guidance.4: Proactive response to convergence; early adopter of AI-SPM/DSPM/runtime convergence
scoring_guidance.5: Market-shaping; first-to-market with CNAPP convergence themes (e.g., Wiz with attack-path graph, Sysdig with runtime CDR)

MKR-03.name: M&A & Strategic Investment Track Record
MKR-03.expanded_definition: Recent acquisitions, strategic investments, or integrations that filled CNAPP capability gaps (e.g., Palo Alto + Dig Security, CrowdStrike + Bionic/Flow Security, Tenable + Ermetic, Fortinet + Lacework).

scoring_guidance.1: No acquisition or investment activity documented
scoring_guidance.2: Minimal M&A; 1 small acquisition in last 3 years
scoring_guidance.3: Strategic acquisitions that filled capability gaps; clear investment thesis
scoring_guidance.4: Multiple strategic acquisitions integrated successfully; strong M&A track record (e.g., Palo Alto's Bridgecrew/Dig)
scoring_guidance.5: Transformative M&A strategy; major acquisitions reshaping market position; integration excellence documented

MKR-04.name: Customer-Driven Feature Delivery
MKR-04.expanded_definition: Evidence the vendor incorporates CNAPP customer feedback into product development — feature request portals, customer advisory boards, transparent roadmaps.
what_to_verify_publicly: Community Slack/forums with product team engagement

scoring_guidance.1: No customer feedback mechanisms visible
scoring_guidance.2: Basic feedback collection; no evidence of incorporation
scoring_guidance.3: Documented advisory board or feedback portal; some features attributed to customer input
scoring_guidance.4: Active community Slack/forum; roadmap influenced by customer input; feature voting visible
scoring_guidance.5: Transparent roadmap tied to customer feedback; documented request-to-delivery metrics; co-development programs

MKE-01.name: Brand Awareness & Cloud-Security Market Presence
MKE-01.expanded_definition: Brand recognition in the CNAPP / cloud-security market, media mentions, social media presence (X, LinkedIn), and overall visibility at cloud-security events.

scoring_guidance.1: Minimal market presence; few media mentions
scoring_guidance.2: Some recognition in niche CNAPP segments; limited media coverage
scoring_guidance.3: Recognized brand in cloud security; regular media coverage; active social presence
scoring_guidance.4: Strong brand with high awareness; frequent mentions; significant social following; conference keynotes
scoring_guidance.5: Top-of-mind brand in CNAPP (e.g., Wiz, Palo Alto Prisma Cloud); extensive media presence; thought leader status

MKE-02.name: Content & Cloud-Threat Research Leadership
MKE-02.expanded_definition: Quality and volume of published cloud-security content: cloud-threat research reports (Wiz Threat Research, Unit 42 Cloud Threat Report, Sysdig Threat Research), blogs, whitepapers, and educational resources.
what_to_verify_publicly: Blog post frequency and depth on cloud threats
Annual Cloud Threat / Cloud Attack reports

scoring_guidance.1: No meaningful content publication
scoring_guidance.2: Sparse blog content; occasional white papers
scoring_guidance.3: Regular content cadence; multiple content types; some original cloud-threat research
scoring_guidance.4: Prolific content publisher; named threat research team; annual cloud-threat report; widely cited
scoring_guidance.5: Best-in-class content engine; flagship annual cloud-threat report cited by media/analysts; influential blog setting market narrative

MKE-03.name: Event & Conference Presence
MKE-03.expanded_definition: Presence at major cloud-security events (RSA, AWS re:Inforce, AWS re:Invent, KubeCon, Black Hat, fwd:cloudsec), own-hosted events, and community engagement.
what_to_verify_publicly: Conference speaker slots at AWS re:Inforce, KubeCon, RSA
Booth presence at major cloud events
Own annual user conference (e.g., Wiz Velocity, PANW Ignite)

scoring_guidance.1: No event presence documented
scoring_guidance.2: Attends 1-2 events per year; booth presence only
scoring_guidance.3: Regular presence at major cloud events; some speaking slots
scoring_guidance.4: Major presence at top-tier events (RSA, re:Inforce, KubeCon); keynote speakers; own user conference
scoring_guidance.5: Dominant event presence; headline sponsor at RSA/re:Inforce; flagship annual conference with 1000+ attendees (e.g., PANW Ignite, Wiz Velocity)

MKE-04.name: Digital Presence & Messaging Clarity
MKE-04.expanded_definition: Website quality, messaging clarity around CNAPP convergence, value proposition articulation, and digital marketing sophistication in a crowded category.

scoring_guidance.1: Poor website; unclear messaging; no differentiation articulated
scoring_guidance.2: Functional website; basic messaging; value prop generic ('we secure the cloud')
scoring_guidance.3: Professional website; clear CNAPP positioning; differentiated messaging; good SEO
scoring_guidance.4: Excellent website with strong UX; sharp differentiated messaging; clear competitive positioning; strong SEO
scoring_guidance.5: Best-in-class digital presence; industry-defining messaging (e.g., 'attack path', 'code-to-cloud'); website as primary lead-gen engine

CXQ-01.name: Peer Review Ratings (CNAPP / Cloud Security)
CXQ-01.expanded_definition: Aggregated ratings on Gartner Peer Insights (CNAPP), G2 (Cloud Security category), and other peer review platforms. Overall rating, review count, sentiment.
what_to_verify_publicly: Gartner Peer Insights CNAPP rating and review count
G2 Cloud Security category rating and Grid position
Customers' Choice or G2 Leader badges

scoring_guidance.1: No peer reviews found on any platform
scoring_guidance.2: Few reviews (<10); available on 1 platform only
scoring_guidance.3: Moderate review count (10-50); 4.0+/5.0 average; on 2+ platforms
scoring_guidance.4: Strong review presence (50-200); 4.3+/5.0 average; Customers' Choice or G2 Leader
scoring_guidance.5: Extensive reviews (200+); 4.5+/5.0 average; Gartner Peer Insights Customers' Choice; G2 Grid Leader

CXQ-02.name: Support Quality & Responsiveness
CXQ-02.expanded_definition: CNAPP customer support quality: support tier structure, response time commitments, escalation paths, named TAMs/CSMs, and satisfaction with support across cloud-security findings.
what_to_verify_publicly: Support tier descriptions (e.g., Standard / Premium / Elite)

scoring_guidance.1: No support quality information available
scoring_guidance.2: Basic support structure documented; no SLA specifics
scoring_guidance.3: Tiered support with documented SLAs; dedicated account management mentioned
scoring_guidance.4: 24/7 premium support; documented response times; TAM/CSM assignment; high support ratings
scoring_guidance.5: Best-in-class support; sub-hour response guarantees; proactive customer success; published high support NPS

CXQ-03.name: Onboarding & Time-to-First-Finding
CXQ-03.expanded_definition: Speed and quality of CNAPP onboarding — agentless cloud connector deployment time, first meaningful misconfiguration / threat finding within hours, and ease of multi-cloud onboarding.

scoring_guidance.1: No onboarding information available
scoring_guidance.2: Basic onboarding mentioned; no timeline or process details
scoring_guidance.3: Documented onboarding with milestones; deployment guides; reasonable time-to-value (days)
scoring_guidance.4: Fast agentless onboarding (<1 hour to first findings); structured enablement; deployment automation
scoring_guidance.5: Same-day full multi-cloud onboarding; agentless cloud connector with sub-30-minute time-to-first-finding documented

CXQ-04.name: Customer Success & Expansion
CXQ-04.expanded_definition: Evidence of customer success programs, CNAPP expansion revenue (cross-sell of DSPM, AI-SPM, code-to-cloud modules), customer community, and long-term relationship investment.
what_to_verify_publicly: Community forums or user groups (e.g., Wiz community)

scoring_guidance.1: No customer success program visible
scoring_guidance.2: Basic account management; no proactive success program
scoring_guidance.3: Designated CSM program; QBRs documented; customer training available
scoring_guidance.4: Mature customer success with proactive engagement; customer community; documented expansion revenue
scoring_guidance.5: Best-in-class customer success; advisory boards; published NRR >130% (typical for top CNAPP vendors); active user community

MKU-01.name: Cloud-Security Vision & CNAPP Convergence Direction
MKU-01.expanded_definition: The vendor's articulated view of where CNAPP is heading, how they define platform convergence (CSPM + CWPP + CIEM + DSPM + AI-SPM), and whether their vision aligns with or shapes Gartner's market direction.
what_to_verify_publicly: CEO/CTO interviews and keynotes (e.g., Wiz, PANW, CrowdStrike)

scoring_guidance.1: No market vision articulated
scoring_guidance.2: Generic positioning; follows market without clear vision
scoring_guidance.3: Clear CNAPP perspective; articulated view of cloud-security evolution; some thought leadership
scoring_guidance.4: Strong vision shaping market direction; forward-looking strategy on AI-SPM/DSPM/runtime convergence
scoring_guidance.5: Market-defining vision (e.g., Wiz attack-path graph, PANW Code-to-Cloud); other vendors react to their narrative

MKU-02.name: Product Roadmap & R&D Investment
MKU-02.expanded_definition: Published or implied CNAPP roadmap (DSPM, AI-SPM, runtime, code-to-cloud), R&D investment indicators, and clarity on future capability development.
what_to_verify_publicly: R&D job postings volume and roles
Patent filings on graph analysis / attack paths

scoring_guidance.1: No roadmap or R&D indicators available
scoring_guidance.2: Vague future direction mentioned; minimal R&D signals
scoring_guidance.3: General roadmap themes documented; R&D investment evidenced by hiring and releases
scoring_guidance.4: Detailed roadmap shared with customers; significant R&D investment; patent filings; named research lab
scoring_guidance.5: Transparent multi-year roadmap; R&D >25% of revenue; active patent portfolio on cloud-security innovations; research partnerships

MKU-03.name: Platform & Ecosystem Strategy
MKU-03.expanded_definition: Platform extensibility, API marketplace, integration ecosystem depth (SIEM, SOAR, EDR, ITSM, IaC tools), and strategy for becoming the consolidated CNAPP platform vs. point solution.
what_to_verify_publicly: Developer resources and SDKs (e.g., Wiz CLI, OPA support)

scoring_guidance.1: No platform or ecosystem strategy visible
scoring_guidance.2: Basic integrations; no API documentation; point-solution positioning
scoring_guidance.3: Documented integrations with major SIEM/EDR/IaC tools; API available; growing partner ecosystem
scoring_guidance.4: Rich integration marketplace (50+); documented APIs with SDKs; technology partner program; clear platform positioning
scoring_guidance.5: Open platform with 100+ integrations; developer ecosystem; marketplace adoption; platform is industry standard

VIG-01.name: Vertical-Specific Solutions
VIG-01.expanded_definition: Named vertical/industry solutions (financial services, healthcare, public sector, manufacturing), compliance packages (PCI-DSS, HIPAA, FedRAMP, IL5), and industry-specific cloud-security detections.
what_to_verify_publicly: Compliance certification logos (FedRAMP, HITRUST, IL4/IL5, etc.)

scoring_guidance.1: No vertical differentiation
scoring_guidance.2: Generic compliance mention; no industry-specific solutions
scoring_guidance.3: 2-3 named vertical solutions; FedRAMP Moderate or 1-2 industry compliance packs
scoring_guidance.4: Dedicated offerings for 4+ industries; FedRAMP High / IL4 / HITRUST certified; vertical GTM teams
scoring_guidance.5: Industry leader in 2+ verticals; FedRAMP High + IL5; comprehensive compliance suite; vertical advisory boards

VIG-02.name: Industry Concentration & References
VIG-02.expanded_definition: Customer concentration across verticals, published industry references, and vertical CNAPP market share indicators.

scoring_guidance.1: No vertical customer references
scoring_guidance.2: Customers in 1-2 verticals only
scoring_guidance.3: References across 3-5 verticals; some concentration data available
scoring_guidance.4: Strong presence in 5+ verticals; documented vertical share in at least one industry
scoring_guidance.5: Dominant in 2+ verticals (e.g., financial services, federal); comprehensive vertical portfolio; recognized vertical specialist

VIG-03.name: Regional & Global Cloud Coverage
VIG-03.expanded_definition: Cloud region availability, data residency options (US, EU, APAC), regional compliance (GDPR, DORA, PIPL), GovCloud / sovereign cloud support, and service availability across geographies.
what_to_verify_publicly: GovCloud / Azure Gov / Google Assured Workloads support

scoring_guidance.1: Single country/region coverage only
scoring_guidance.2: Primary region plus limited international availability
scoring_guidance.3: Coverage in 2-3 major regions; some data residency options; GovCloud support
scoring_guidance.4: Global coverage; data residency in US/EU/APAC; AWS GovCloud + Azure Gov support; GDPR/DORA
scoring_guidance.5: True global coverage; sovereign cloud support; comprehensive data residency; FedRAMP High + IL5; global compliance portfolio

VIG-04.name: Localization & Regional Adaptation
VIG-04.expanded_definition: Multi-language support for the CNAPP UI, regional pricing, culturally adapted services, and local cloud-security partner networks (especially APAC, EU).

scoring_guidance.1: English-only; no regional adaptation
scoring_guidance.2: Website in 1-2 additional languages; minimal localization
scoring_guidance.3: Multi-language support (3+); some regional partners; localized documentation
scoring_guidance.4: Comprehensive localization; regional pricing; local partner networks; multi-language support
scoring_guidance.5: Full global localization; local cloud-security teams in major regions; regional GTM; culturally adapted services

mq_scoring_mode.description: Combines CNAPP capability data + MQ Gap scores to produce 15 Magic Quadrant criteria. Each criterion has a formula mapping source data to a 0-5 score.

criteria.formula: Weighted average of CNAPP pillar_scores (CSPM x 0.20, CWPP x 0.18, CIEM x 0.15, SHIFT x 0.12, CDR x 0.15, DSPM x 0.12, FRNG x 0.08)

criteria.source: CNAPP MQ Gap schema — VIA pillar
CNAPP MQ Gap schema — SLE pillar
criteria.gap_supplement: Sales execution research needed; CNAPP lacks dedicated pricing schema today

criteria.source: CNAPP MQ Gap schema — MKR pillar
CNAPP MQ Gap schema — MKE pillar
CNAPP MQ Gap schema — CXQ pillar

criteria.formula: Weighted average of CNAPP operational pillars (CDR x 0.40, CSPM x 0.30, CWPP x 0.30)

criteria.source: CNAPP MQ Gap schema — MKU pillar (MKU-01)
CNAPP MQ Gap schema — MKE pillar (subset)
CNAPP MQ Gap schema — SLE pillar (subset)

criteria.formula: (CNAPP innovation pillars avg [DSPM, FRNG] x 0.50) + (MKU-02 x 0.25) + (MKU-03 x 0.25)
criteria.source: CNAPP capability (DSPM, FRNG) + MQ Gap MKU
CNAPP MQ Gap schema — VIG pillar (subset)

criteria.formula: CNAPP innovation composite (FRNG x 0.40, DSPM x 0.30, CDR x 0.20, SHIFT x 0.10)

criteria.source: CNAPP MQ Gap schema — VIG pillar (subset)
